title: logtrim keeps its cut when flock(1) is absent or times out, so the bash logger trims on Windows and never exits its caller's shell
intention: bin/logger_for_bash logtrim trims when flock is not installed, skips the cut on a flock timeout without ending the caller's shell, and still serialises trims where flock exists.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: test_trim_keeps_the_newest_lines: expected exactly 10 lines after trim, got 201 on Windows; every other case of test_logger_for_bash.py ran green, line-451 trace-wire case included
traces_to: Law 3: the red was measured at 201 lines on Windows and both teeth ran red on the unedited file; Law 7: a diagnostic surface may fail but must never take down the script it observes (the logger's own charter).
how: In logtrim replace `flock -x -w 5 9 || exit 0` with: run flock; on rc 127 (not installed) go on unlocked, on rc 1 (timeout) return 0 from the function, never exit. Red-first proof bin/proofs/test_logtrim_trims_without_flock.py shadows flock with a shell function returning 127 and 1: (1) with 127 the 200-line log is cut to 10 and the caller survives; (2) with 1 the caller survives and no line is cut.

clauses.claim: with flock absent (rc 127) logtrim cuts a 200-line log to 10 and the caller shell survives, where the unedited logger leaves 201 and kills the caller
with flock timing out (rc 1) the caller shell survives and no line is cut, where the unedited logger exits the caller

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.
re-cross BUILDME and PROVEME on Linux: the Windows crossings (their certs stand in CairnCommons/certificates) never reached main's bin/history.json; no code change
